question: Owner request: represent Bill Gates's 'Green Premium' (How to Avoid a Climate Disaster) by activity, using only open, primary, traceable sources.
need: The extra cost of the zero-carbon way of doing something compared with the fossil way, by activity: electricity, cement, steel, plastics and chemicals, aviation fuel, shipping, trucking and cars, heating (heat pump vs gas boiler), and farming and food (green vs grey ammonia, meat alternatives vs beef). Costs appear only as system-level facts with a named source (docs/style.md: no savings, payback, tariff or investment framing; a negative premium is described as 'costs less to produce/run per unit', never as a saving for the reader). The website never computes a number. A difference or ratio may be computed in the pipeline only when the clean and fossil inputs share source, vintage, currency year, unit and basis (same region, year, discount rate, carbon-price and subsidy treatment). Strong preference for producers that publish the premium itself, or both costs on one basis, in a downloadable table. Licence comes from the producer's own terms; material a report attributes to third parties (BNEF, S&P/Platts, Argus, Wood Mackenzie, JATO, ICIS, CRU, IHS, paid IEA data) is excluded even inside an open report. Gates's own Green Premium figures come from Breakthrough Energy, whose terms rule them out, so premiums have to be assembled from other producers activity by activity.
method: Fetched on 2026-10-08 with curl (browser user agent) and pdftotext/openpyxl; no host blocks were worked around (iea.org HTML, mdpi.com, ScienceDirect, RSC, ACS, Cell, energy-transitions.org, gatesnotes.com and transportenvironment.org refuse scripts; their terms were read from web.archive.org copies or repository copies of the publisher PDF, as stated per candidate). Already-registered sources (irena-costs-2025, drawdown-explorer) were read from the repo's own snapshots in pipeline/.snapshots. Three research sub-agents covered IEA reports, NGO and think-tank reports, and peer-reviewed papers; their key claims for ETP 2026, the CEMCAP cement table and the ICCT truck figure were spot-checked against the downloaded text. Values quoted as 'text' are sentences in the report, not table cells.

open_questions: Rule 7: IEA chart-library and chapter pages embed the plotted series (data-chart-csv attribute, credited 'IEA. Licence: CC BY 4.0') while marking them 'not available for download', and iea.org blocks scripts, so they were read from Internet Archive copies. Is reading published chart data from an archived page acceptable, or should the owner ask the IEA (rights@iea.org) for ETP 2026 Fig 7.15 and Fig 2.15, GHR 2026 Chapter 4 and Future of Heat Pumps Fig 3.1 data?

Quoted statements: most open premiums for steel, cement, ammonia and shipping are sentences with ranges in IEA reports, not table cells. Should these be published as quoted statements with page references (as energy-institute-review-2026 is), and how does check-build verify a kicker against a quote on refresh?

Same-basis rule versus carbon prices and subsidies: DESNZ fossil totals include a UK carbon cost; EIA totals after credits include US tax and 45Q credits; IEA ranges are sometimes with and without USD 100-150/t CO2. Decide one convention (e.g. always before carbon price and subsidies, using the published component columns) before computing any difference.
Share-alike sources (ICCT, RMI): RMI's CC BY-SA statement conflicts with 'All rights reserved' on the back cover; confirm with RMI. ICCT is handled as in icct-lca-2025.

Producer models with third-party inputs: the European Hydrogen Observatory's electrolysis cost uses BNEF capex; Devlin et al. 2023 uses TransitionZero for the blast-furnace comparator; ICCT truck TCO uses DKV diesel prices. Is a producer's own computed value acceptable when one input is third-party, or only when the published value itself is unattributed?
Supplementary data licences: Springer Nature source-data files (Devlin 2023) and MDPI supplements carry no licence text; confirm they fall under the article's CC BY.
IPCC AR6 WGIII Figure SPM.7 data (doi:10.48490/ayfg-tv12): DataCite has no rights statement and the catalogue is not script-readable; a person should check its licence in a browser.
Gates Notes and Energy Transitions Commission terms need a manual browser check (both block scripts); both are expected to be unusable.

Not yet checked: NREL Annual Technology Baseline (NREL renamed; atb.nrel.gov no longer resolves from here), Link et al. 2024 Nature Energy (truck TCO, CC BY per Crossref), Wilson et al. 2024 Joule (heat pumps, CC BY per Crossref), Fasihi et al. 2021 Applied Energy (green ammonia, CC BY per Crossref), Humbird 2021 and Risner et al. 2021 (cultivated meat, CC BY per Crossref), Lopez et al. 2023 EES (chemicals, CC BY 3.0). Their values and input attributions were not read.

Framing: several sources show negative premiums (heat pumps, electric cars and trucks over a lifetime, new renewables). The style rule forbids savings framing; the dashboard needs wording such as 'costs X less per megawatt-hour of heat to supply, on Drawdown's estimate' and must avoid per-household or per-reader amounts.

Gates's book defines premiums at market prices without carbon pricing and often as a percentage of the product price. None of the open sources reproduces his table; the dashboard should say it shows other producers' estimates of the same idea, not Gates's figures.
